callout_cancellation.remove_scope: first matching callback/context in ready queue preferred, else delayed queue; no own scan/wait of in-flight counter 0x1e7264; not proof of caller lifetime safety
callout_cancellation.callback_abi: worker pushes second argument entry or NULL, then first argument saved context; PC callbacks read only EBP+8; original delayed->ready promotion and runtime reachability remain open
callout_cancellation.spin_scope: raw MOV; TEST register; JNZ same TEST. If captured nonzero and no exceptional state/register change, backedge does not reload lock memory. C memory-poll loop is not literal own instruction behavior.

local_findings: PCresume schedules before R+0x48=1 and sets CR0|8; monitor clears R+0x48 before deliver and also sets CR0|8. Both CR0 changes absent from C.
Monitor snapshot flags reflect virtual IF from R+0x68 then OR R+0x70&0x7000 without first clearing snapshot bits 0x7000. Actual monitor flags clear TF/DF/VM only by 0xfffdfaff.
FA/FC gate selector bit4 only; FD forces VM flags and clears ordinary segment slots without own writes to VM tail. Actual selected IRETD consumes active-thread state, not an explicit S argument.

PCcreate maps caller task and attaches wrapper to port-converted target thread. Post-map copyout failure own path deallocates thread and returns4 without own vm_map_remove. Wired allocator result not tested in own caller; callee guarantees not assumed.
PCdestroy own order user pmap/map removal -> map deallocate -> cancelall -> wired free -> wrapper free; no own PCB+ec clear. Caller PCB lifetime and callback quiescence unresolved.
Timer2 expired bit generated only while R+48 active; Timer4 has no active gate. Both clear armed bit when armed. cancel functions do not themselves clear record flags.

PCscheduleTimers scales in DWORD then passes zero high DWORD; dispatch disabled gate can return without enqueue while caller subsequently sets armed bit. Whether gate can be disabled at PC use is unresolved.

calloutRemove cannot find already-dequeued callback by scanning these queues. Worker increments in-flight counter before unlock, invokes saved callback/context, then decrements. Remove has no own in-flight wait; no claim that actual unsafe interleaving occurs.
PCexception pushes continuation pointer, CR2, status,1 before exception call and removes16 stack bytes; C shows two arguments. Callee semantic signature and continuation lifecycle still open.
Prior96 frame-initialization omissions remain linked in bounded ledger; not silently repaired and not a whole-kernel decompiler ledger.
